passages.title: Creation
passages.summary: God creates the world and gives humans care of its life. God calls creation good. Human life has worth. Care for the earth follows from God's gift.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: Moses 2 places human creation within God's work. Human dignity shapes how we treat others.

passages.title: Life in the garden
passages.summary: God rests. God places the man in Eden and forms the woman. Rest, work, and partnership belong to human life. The garden also includes a command.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: Moses 3 connects the garden with God's commands. Study work, rest, and partnership together.

passages.title: The Fall
passages.summary: The man and woman eat the forbidden fruit. They leave the garden. Their choice brings loss and responsibility. God still clothes them.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: Moses 4 expands the garden account. Second Nephi 2 connects the Fall with choice and redemption.

passages.title: Cain and Abel
passages.summary: Cain kills Abel. The chapter follows Cain's family and the birth of Seth. Anger can destroy family bonds. Cain's question tests our care for other people.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: Moses 5 adds gospel teaching after the Fall. Compare Cain's choices with Adam and Eve's worship.

passages.title: Generations to Noah
passages.summary: The family record traces Adam's line to Noah. Enoch walks with God. Death repeats through the record. Enoch's account introduces hope within that pattern.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: Moses 6–7 expands Enoch's account. Zion means a people united in righteousness and care.

passages.title: Noah builds the ark
passages.summary: Violence fills the earth. God tells Noah to build an ark. Noah responds to God's warning with action. The story connects judgment with preservation.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: Moses 8 describes Noah's preaching before the flood. Read preparation alongside the call to repent.

passages.title: The flood
passages.summary: Noah's household and the animals enter the ark. The flood covers the land. The narrative depicts loss on a great scale. Preservation remains part of the story.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: The Church manual reads Noah's deliverance within God's dealings with humanity. Consider faithful action under warning.

passages.title: The waters recede
passages.summary: The ark rests in the mountains of Ararat. Noah leaves and builds an altar. Noah responds to deliverance with worship. The promise concerns the world's continuing seasons.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Noah worships after deliverance. Consider how gratitude can follow a period of waiting.

passages.title: A covenant with Noah
passages.summary: God gives the rainbow as a covenant sign. Noah's sons receive different blessings. The covenant includes living creatures. The chapter also warns against bloodshed.
passages.uncertainty: No verified location is supplied for this chapter.

lds.text: A covenant is a sacred agreement. God's sign joins a promise with duties toward life.

passages.title: Families and nations
passages.summary: The chapter lists peoples descended from Noah's sons. The list links Israel's story to many peoples. It expresses kinship through family lines.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: The family record joins many peoples to common ancestors. Consider the duties that shared humanity creates.

passages.title: Babel and Terah's family
passages.summary: People build Babel. God confuses their speech. Terah's family travels from Ur toward Canaan. Babel questions human attempts to secure greatness. Terah's family prepares the next story.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: The Church manual contrasts Babel with the covenant family story. Consider how pride differs from trust.

passages.title: Abram's call
passages.summary: Abram travels from Haran to Canaan. Famine leads him into Egypt. The promise extends blessing beyond one household. Abram's fear also exposes others to danger.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Abraham 2 links the covenant with blessing all families. Study the promise as a duty to serve.

passages.title: Abram and Lot separate
passages.summary: Abram lets Lot choose land. Lot settles near Sodom. God renews Abram's promise. Abram chooses peace over a dispute. Land and descendants remain central to the promise.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Abraham gives Lot the first choice. Consider how covenant living can support peace over advantage.

passages.title: Lot rescued
passages.summary: Abram rescues Lot after a battle. Melchizedek blesses Abram. Abram rejects wealth from Sodom. Melchizedek connects blessing with worship of God.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Alma 13 expands Melchizedek's role as a priest. Keep that teaching distinct from Genesis's brief account.

passages.title: God's covenant with Abram
passages.summary: God promises descendants to Abram. A covenant ceremony follows. Abram trusts despite his lack of an heir. The promise includes future suffering and return.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: God's promise meets Abraham's fear about an heir. Consider how faith can coexist with unanswered questions.

passages.title: Hagar and Ishmael
passages.summary: Hagar flees harsh treatment from Sarai. God's messenger meets her. Ishmael is born. God sees a woman in distress. Her story challenges indifference toward vulnerable people.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: God sees Hagar in distress. Consider whose need you can recognize within unequal relationships.

passages.title: New names and covenant
passages.summary: God names Abraham and Sarah. Circumcision becomes a covenant sign. God promises Isaac. The covenant sets duties for the household. God also promises to bless Ishmael.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Abraham 2 links covenant blessings with the gospel. Study both the promised blessing and its responsibility.

passages.title: Visitors and Abraham's plea
passages.summary: Visitors promise Sarah a son. Abraham pleads for Sodom. Hospitality opens the story. Abraham's questions explore justice and mercy.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Abraham pleads for other people's lives. Consider how prayer can express care beyond your household.

passages.title: Sodom and Lot's escape
passages.summary: Lot hosts visitors. A violent crowd threatens them. Lot's household escapes Sodom. The account condemns violence and abuse of guests. Escape does not end the household's troubles.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Lot's escape includes grief and later family harm. Deliverance does not remove the need for moral care.

passages.title: Abraham and Abimelech
passages.summary: Abraham calls Sarah his sister. God warns Abimelech in a dream. Fear leads to deception. The account shows how that deception harms other people.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Abraham's fear puts Sarah at risk. Consider the effects of choices made to protect yourself.

passages.title: Isaac and Ishmael
passages.summary: Isaac is born. Hagar and Ishmael leave. God provides water. Abraham makes a treaty. Both sons receive God's care. Family conflict does not erase Hagar's need or Ishmael's promise.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: God hears Hagar and Ishmael. Family conflict must not erase another person's need.

passages.title: The binding of Isaac
passages.summary: God tests Abraham. A messenger stops the sacrifice. A ram takes Isaac's place. The narrative presents trust under severe strain. God stops the killing of Isaac.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Jacob 4:5 links Abraham's offering with the Father's gift of Christ. Genesis itself stops Isaac's sacrifice.

passages.title: Sarah's burial
passages.summary: Sarah dies. Abraham buys the field and cave of Machpelah. The purchase gives Abraham a burial place. The promised land first becomes a family grave.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Abraham secures a burial place for Sarah. Consider how covenant hope can accompany mourning.

passages.title: Rebekah meets Isaac
passages.summary: Abraham's servant seeks a wife for Isaac. Rebekah agrees to travel. Rebekah shows care through action. Her consent matters in the journey to Isaac.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Rebekah agrees to the journey. Consider the place of willingness within family and covenant choices.

passages.title: Abraham's death and the twins
passages.summary: Abraham dies. Rebekah bears Esau and Jacob. Esau sells his birthright. Family promises pass to another generation. Immediate hunger and lasting inheritance come into conflict.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: The birthright concerns a lasting family responsibility. Consider what you value beyond an immediate need.

passages.title: Isaac's wells
passages.summary: Isaac lives near Gerar. Disputes arise over wells. God renews the promise. Water supports life and creates conflict. Isaac moves rather than continuing each dispute.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: God renews the promise to Isaac. Consider how patient action can reduce a dispute.

passages.title: Jacob receives the blessing
passages.summary: Rebekah and Jacob deceive Isaac. Esau loses the blessing and threatens Jacob. A family promise unfolds through deception and grief. The chapter does not hide their harmful choices.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Jacob receives a blessing through deception. A promised purpose does not make every family choice harmless.

passages.title: Jacob's dream at Bethel
passages.summary: Jacob leaves for Haran. At Bethel he dreams of a stairway reaching heaven. God meets Jacob during his flight. Jacob responds with a vow.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: God meets Jacob while he travels away from home. Consider your response to God's promised presence.

passages.title: Leah and Rachel
passages.summary: Jacob meets Rachel. Laban substitutes Leah at the wedding. Jacob also marries Rachel. Deception returns within Jacob's life. God sees Leah's distress and gives her children.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: God sees Leah's pain. Consider how unequal affection can affect people within a family.

passages.title: Jacob's growing household
passages.summary: Rachel, Leah, Bilhah, and Zilpah bear children. Jacob's flocks increase. The account includes rivalry and unequal power. The mothers' words reveal their hopes and pain.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: The children's names reveal hope and distress. Consider each mother's experience rather than only the family totals.

passages.title: Jacob leaves Laban
passages.summary: Jacob's household leaves Haran. Laban pursues them. They make an agreement. The household seeks freedom from Laban's control. A boundary helps end their dispute.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Jacob and Laban set a boundary. Consider how clear agreements can help end harmful disputes.

passages.title: Jacob wrestles
passages.summary: Jacob prepares to meet Esau. He wrestles through the night and receives the name Israel. Jacob faces fear and dependence. His new name marks a lasting change.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Jacob receives the name Israel after a struggle. Consider how dependence on God can accompany fear.

passages.title: Jacob and Esau meet
passages.summary: Esau embraces Jacob. Jacob settles near Shechem. The meeting interrupts expected revenge. Gifts and humility support renewed peace.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Esau welcomes Jacob. Consider what reconciliation requires after years of injury.

passages.title: Dinah and Shechem
passages.summary: Shechem violates Dinah. Her brothers kill the town's men after a deceptive agreement. The narrative exposes sexual violence and violent revenge. Neither harm should disappear from the reading.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Dinah suffers violence and her brothers take revenge. Consider how to protect people without adding further harm.

passages.title: Return to Bethel
passages.summary: Jacob returns to Bethel. Rachel dies near Bethlehem. Isaac dies. Worship, birth, and death shape the family's return. The promise continues through grief.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Jacob returns to worship amid family loss. Consider how faith and grief can remain present together.

passages.title: Esau's descendants
passages.summary: The chapter records Esau's family and rulers in Edom. Esau's line receives space in the story. Israel's neighbors also have a history.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Esau's descendants have their own place in Genesis. Consider how to read neighbors without dismissing them.

passages.title: Joseph sold
passages.summary: Joseph's brothers sell him. Traders take him to Egypt. Jacob mourns. Favoritism and jealousy fracture the family. Joseph's loss begins the journey toward Egypt.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Joseph loses home through his brothers' choices. Consider the damage caused by favoritism and envy.

passages.title: Judah and Tamar
passages.summary: Judah fails to provide for Tamar. Tamar acts to preserve her family claim. Judah admits his failure. The story exposes his unequal judgment of Tamar.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

lds.text: Judah admits that Tamar has a stronger claim. Consider whether your judgment uses unequal standards.

passages.title: Joseph in Potiphar's house
passages.summary: Joseph serves Potiphar. Potiphar's wife falsely accuses Joseph. He enters prison. Joseph keeps his integrity despite pressure. His imprisonment is not evidence of guilt.
passages.uncertainty: Lines connect named places. They do not trace a surveyed ancient road.

guides.title: Study Genesis
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: Creation
steps.text: God creates the world and gives humans care of its life. God calls creation good. Human life has worth. Care for the earth follows from God's gift.

steps.title: Isaac's wells
steps.text: Isaac lives near Gerar. Disputes arise over wells. God renews the promise. Water supports life and creates conflict. Isaac moves rather than continuing each dispute.

steps.title: Burial and forgiveness
steps.text: Joseph buries Jacob in Canaan. He reassures his brothers. Joseph later dies in Egypt. Forgiveness does not deny the brothers' evil. Joseph's burial request points toward a future return.
